clue.text: Cynical and ill, maybe, in a way that describes bad depression

definitions.text: in a way that describes bad depression

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the two words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone both cynical and ill is a picture of a gloomy state of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' tells you to rearrange the letters of CYNICAL and ILL together; 'and' only joins them. Severe depression is called clinical depression.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious depression diagnosed by a doctor is termed clinical, so a sufferer is described as depressed in that medical manner.

clue.text: Sign of wheat crop on island

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits after it

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a cereal crop such as wheat

explanation.surface: A field of wheat growing on an island is taken as an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat is one of the twelve zodiac signs, the tenth of the star signs.

clue.text: I have little time for US composer

parts.note: contracted, I have is written I've
S is the abbreviation for second, a little time

explanation.surface: Someone impatient admits they have no time for an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer, known for The Unanswered Question.

clue.text: One civil engineer certain to be hemmed in by the weather

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: A civil engineer is sure to be trapped by bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or harbour frozen fast by winter ice is trapped by the cold conditions.

clue.text: Woman who is an idiot in motoring organisation

indicators.note: in says the idiot is placed inside the motoring organisation

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring breakdown service
a nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish woman works for a breakdown service.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, Britain's big roadside rescue club.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: The French male getting married needs space

parts.note: le is French for the
a groom is the man at a wedding

explanation.surface: A French bridegroom needs room for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Room for the legs in a vehicle or seat row is a kind of space.

clue.text: Following afternoon meal, has late one on ship (it's not rough)

indicators.note: on ship means aboard, so the meal pieces sit inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: following says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: tea is a light British meal taken in the afternoon
to dine is to have a late meal, the evening one

explanation.surface: After tea, a passenger has a late supper on a liner, hoping the sea stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' and 'on' are the two placing signals: on a ship means aboard it, so everything else goes inside. The definition reads as a cryptic aside: calm seas are the opposite of rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmness and stability are the opposite of rough motion, so the quality is what a calm sea has.

clue.text: Threaten little devil with death

parts.note: an imp is a small devil
end can mean death

explanation.surface: A mischievous imp threatens someone with death.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom or be about to happen, as danger does, is to menace.

clue.text: Watch period composition 23

parts.note: time means a period, as in a time of plenty
a piece is a musical or written composition

explanation.surface: Watch out for a period composition.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '23' plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch is a portable clock, a device for telling the hour.

clue.text: One gets a turn for this role

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: An actor gets a turn at a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's villain in Othello is a famous stage part.

clue.text: A Roman law is designed for a man or woman

parts.note: lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A Roman statute is drafted to apply to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A given name used for both sexes, so it fits either a boy or a girl.

clue.text: Murphy & Co using a lot of money when getting in something digital

indicators.note: getting in says the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal
a toe is a digit of the foot, so it is a thing that is digital

explanation.surface: A firm called Murphy and Company spends a fortune on a digital gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is Irish slang for a potato, so Murphy & Co are spuds in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is an old slang name for the spud, so the name and its companions are those tubers.

clue.text: Chant by man drinking drinks from Sri Lanka

indicators.note: by means beside, so the chant comes next to the rest

parts.note: to chant is to sing

indicators.note: drinking says the drinks go inside the man

parts.note: he stands for a man
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A man chants beside someone drinking beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest ethnic group of Ceylon and its language bear this name, so it means native to that island.

clue.text: Cross province from east without being exposed to the elements

definitions.text: without being exposed to the elements

indicators.note: read from east means right to left, so the whole run is written backwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix in a church
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a province travelling west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from east' turns the whole of ROOD and NI backwards; NI is Northern Ireland, known in Britain as the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: Under a roof, inside a building, shelter keeps off rain and wind.

clue.text: Battle, one after which King's captured in unusual manner

indicators.note: after which says what follows comes after the first piece

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: captured says the king is held inside the scrambled letters
unusual means the letters of manner are arranged oddly

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A king is taken prisoner in strange fashion after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges MANNER to NERMAN, 'captured' puts K inside it, and 'after which' places the result after I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Crimean War engagement of 1854, fought near Sevastopol.

clue.text: Good mike's playing up, producing effect that's husky

indicators.note: playing up means misbehaving, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A good microphone acting up makes the singer sound hoarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing up' rearranges GOOD and MIKES; 'husky' is not hoarse here but the sled dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The husky is an Arctic sledge dog, bred by the Inuit.

clue.text: To do with measurement of people's range

parts.note: men's means belonging to people
the Urals are a mountain range in Russia

explanation.surface: Measuring the size of a people's mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin mensura, it describes measuring, especially musical time.

clue.text: Applied scientist presenting Flying Scotsman to the Queen?

parts.note: the Flying Scotsman is a famous steam locomotive
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A famous train is presented to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Scotsman is a celebrated British steam locomotive; ER is the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who designs machines and structures puts science into practical use.

clue.text: What it brings to the cooker maybe natural

definitions.text: What it brings to the cooker maybe natural

parts.words: What it brings to the cooker maybe natural
parts.note: the pipe that delivers fuel, possibly natural gas, to a stove

explanation.surface: Something natural supplied to a kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground supply pipe carries fuel from the utility to household appliances.

clue.text: Outline picture of second boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture of a second boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing gives only the outlines of a scene.

clue.text: Bird involved in winter celebrations

indicators.note: involved in says the answer is tucked within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird takes part in midwinter festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: A male hawk, especially a peregrine, used in falconry.

clue.text: South American money, we hear — Hitchcock's speciality

parts.note: US means American

indicators.note: we hear says the money word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: pence are British coins, small money

explanation.surface: Hitchcock's specialty was talk of South American cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock, the master of the thriller, specialised in tense anticipation.

clue.text: Part of arm needed for some novel bowing

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cellist's fresh bowing technique depends on the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint in the middle of the arm is needed for bowing a violin.

clue.text: Having no ethical standards in American exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A test given in the United States is unprincipled.
explanation.definitionFit: Without morals means neither good nor bad, outside ethics.

clue.text: Writer, a monkey, a bit ironic, some say

indicators.note: some say tells you the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: sarky is British slang for sarcastic, somewhat ironic

explanation.surface: A writer calls a monkey slightly sarcastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Three readings: Saki was H. H. Munro's pen name, the saki is a South American monkey, and the word sounds like sarky (sarcastic) in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of short-story author H. H. Munro, and also a long-tailed monkey of Amazonian forests.

clue.text: Clothing to boast about

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Showing off about one's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments, especially distinctive dress, as in clerical outfits.

clue.text: Give new directions to understand garment

parts.note: to read is to understand, as in read a situation
a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: Instructions to grasp how to put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To change the address on a letter so it goes elsewhere.

clue.text: Essentially permanent and secure at home?

explanation.surface: Something is permanently, safely at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherent and lasting describes an inner presence; read as two words it says inside a house.
